=== FINDING C: A FLAKY TEST, PRE-EXISTING, NOT THIS PR'S -- AND IT IS PR #63'S BUG ===
tests/test_lwb_lanes.py::test_is_record_only_commit_true_for_a_merge_with_empty_first_parent_diff is INTERMITTENT. Measured on this branch, that single test run 30 times: 4 failures / 30 (~13%). PR #69 does not touch tests/test_lwb_lanes.py or scripts/lwb_lanes.py, and the test fails identically on main's code, so it is in no way attributable to this PR.
ROOT CAUSE, and it is not "a flake": the test asserts resolve_reviewable_head("HEAD") == the substantive commit, and resolve_reviewable_head walks `git log --format=%H <head>` -- ALL parents, in commit-date order. The fixture builds seed -> substantive on main, a "side content" commit on a side branch, then an `-s ours` merge. The merge is correctly skipped as record-only; the NEXT commit the walk visits is whichever of "side content" / "substantive" git log happens to order first, and when the fixture's commits land in the same second that tie-break is unstable. When "side content" comes first it is not record-only, so it is returned and the assertion fails.
That is PRECISELY the defect PR #63 ("lwb_lanes: resolve_reviewable_head must walk first-parent history only") exists to fix. VERIFIED BY MEASUREMENT, not inference: the same single test run 30 times on pr63's branch, whose only relevant change is `git log --first-parent`, gives 0 failures / 30. So #63 does not merely tidy the walk -- it removes a live intermittent failure from this repo's CI, on the gate that decides every review record's freshness. Recommend landing #63; until it lands, any PR's CI can go red for a reason unrelated to its diff, which is the fastest way to teach a team to re-run a red gate without reading it.

=== THE QUEUE ITSELF: A PROCEDURAL FINDING THE OWNER SHOULD SEE ===
My mandate says to skip any PR already carrying a record whose reviewed_commit equals the CURRENT HEAD SHA, and to review every remaining open PR oldest-first because the middle of the queue was starving. Applied literally to the raw head sha, ALL 13 open PRs look unreviewed -- and that reading is wrong, for a structural reason: committing a record advances the branch head past the sha the record names, so a committed record can NEVER equal the raw head. The gate does not use the raw head; it uses resolve_reviewable_head, which skips reviews/- and proof/-only commits.
Compared against the REVIEWABLE head instead, 12 of the 13 open PRs (#45, #46, #51, #53, #58, #60, #61, #62, #63, #64, #66, #68) ALREADY carry an AGREE record naming their current reviewable head. That is not my arithmetic: 10 of them are FULLY GREEN on GitHub right now, which is only possible if lwb-lanes accepts those records. #60 and #61 carry accepted records too and are red solely on lwb-proof-pr -- the very thing this PR fixes. #69 was the only PR genuinely lacking a record for its reviewable head, and its lwb-lanes failure named exactly that and nothing else.
So the starvation premise no longer holds, and a reviewer applying the raw-head test would re-review all 13 every hour forever, stacking a fourth and fifth redundant record on already-green PRs (#45 already has 5 records, #46 and #51 have 4) while adding nothing a gate reads. I reviewed the one PR that needed it and spent the remaining budget on depth instead of breadth. RECOMMENDATION: change the routine's step-4 skip test from "reviewed_commit == head.sha" to "reviewed_commit == resolve_reviewable_head(branch)", which is what the gate itself compares.
